title: The Missing Parish
premise: When the coffin of San Isidro's beloved founder is exhumed for a centennial reburial and found empty, cathedral archivist Felix Reyes is the only person who ever catalogued the crypt — making him both prime witness and prime suspect. As Felix digs through a century of parish records, he discovers the founder never existed as history remembers him: the town was built on a stolen identity, and someone alive today will kill to keep that inheritance intact. The killer, it turns out, has been feeding Felix curated documents all along, using his own archive against him. In the end, Felix stages a false exhumation of a second grave to force the killer — the parish's own deacon, heir to the founder's true name — into the crypt, where the truth is sealed in writing before the trial begins.
about_author: W. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former diocesan records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing parish archives along the coast before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about paper trails, small towns, and the things people bury on purpose.

chapters.title: The Centennial Order
chapters.summary: Felix Reyes, cathedral archivist, receives the court order authorizing the founder's exhumation for the centennial reburial. His POV establishes his obsessive love of records and his quiet grief over his late partner. The emotional beat is unease: he alone knows the crypt ledger has a page torn out.

chapters.title: Empty Linings
chapters.summary: The exhumation draws the whole town. When the coffin is opened before the crowd, it holds only river stones. Felix watches the mayor's face collapse and notices Deacon Ambrose Salas watching him instead. POV alternates between Felix and Detective Ibarra. The beat is public shock curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: A Ledger With Teeth
chapters.summary: Ibarra interviews Felix, who admits he catalogued the crypt in 2009 and cannot account for one missing hour. Under pressure, Felix hides the fact that his own signature appears on a transfer form he never signed. The beat: fear of being framed by his own meticulous work.

chapters.title: The Founder's Face
chapters.summary: Felix researches founder Emiliano Vidal and finds no photograph predating 1931 — odd for a man so beloved. An anonymous note in his pigeonhole quotes his own catalogue verbatim. Whose POV: Felix, with a brief Ibarra scene. Beat: the case file knows him better than he knows himself.

chapters.title: Salt in the Registers
chapters.summary: Felix discovers baptismal entries altered in matching ink across three decades, all in Vidal's favor. He confides in Marisol, the conservator he's falling for, breaking his rule about sharing archive secrets. Beat: love beginning to outweigh professional isolation.

chapters.title: What the Stones Weigh
chapters.summary: Ibarra traces the river stones to a quarry closed in 1968; whoever filled the coffin knew old local geography intimately. Suspicion falls on the elderly sexton, who dies of an apparent heart attack the same night. Beat: the first death raises stakes from scandal to murder.

chapters.title: The Sexton's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Felix finds the sexton's hidden notebook: a list of graves 'moved' in 1974, including Vidal's. Ibarra rules the death natural, but Felix sees the notebook pages were handled by someone wearing archival cotton gloves. Beat: dread — the killer works inside the church.

chapters.title: Marisol's Hands
chapters.summary: Marisol restores a damaged portrait from the parish house and uncovers a second face painted beneath Vidal's. She and Felix grow closer over the discovery, but she becomes a target when the portrait vanishes overnight. Beat: tenderness shadowed by danger.

chapters.title: Two Men, One Name
chapters.summary: Felix reconstructs the truth: the real Emiliano Vidal died young; a drifter took his name and built the town on his fortune. The inheritance — land, endowments, the parish itself — flows legally to whoever holds the name. Beat: the theme of identity crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Trial Date
chapters.summary: The prosecutor announces the coffin case goes to trial in six weeks, naming Felix a material witness — and quietly, a suspect. Ibarra warns Felix off the archive. Defiant, Felix begins copying everything. Beat: duty versus self-preservation.

chapters.title: Ambrose's Sermon
chapters.summary: Deacon Salas preaches on honoring the dead, quoting a private phrase from the sexton's notebook that was never made public. Felix realizes the deacon read it — or wrote it. Beat: cold recognition disguised as reverence.

chapters.title: The Curated Trail
chapters.summary: Felix maps every document the anonymous notes led him to and realizes they form a deliberate path — someone has been archiving the investigation itself, steering him. Marisol helps him date the forgeries. Beat: the hunter understands he is also the quarry.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Dust
chapters.summary: Land records show the Vidal estate passes to the parish if the bloodline ends — meaning the deacon controls everything upon proof of no heirs. Felix finds a sealed 1974 letter hinting a descendant lives. Beat: motive sharpens into something worth killing for.

chapters.title: Break-In at the Crypt
chapters.summary: Someone ransacks the crypt office and burns the duplicate registers; Felix arrives mid-fire and saves one scorched folio, burning his hands. Ibarra finally believes him. Beat: sacrifice converts doubt into alliance.

chapters.title: The Descendant
chapters.summary: Following the 1974 letter, Felix locates an aging woman in the next county — Vidal's granddaughter, living under another name, terrified. She gives him her grandfather's true burial site: not the crypt, but unconsecrated ground. Beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Confession Booth
chapters.summary: Salas offers Felix absolution-adjacent friendship, probing what he knows. Felix lies smoothly for the first time in his life and hates how easily it comes. Beat: moral erosion in service of justice; love against duty inverts — duty now serves love of truth.

chapters.title: Second Grave
chapters.summary: Felix, Ibarra, and Marisol secretly exhume the true grave and find remains plus a locket proving the identity swap. But the site is watched; their permit trail was leaked. Someone knows. Beat: triumph immediately poisoned.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Marisol disappears; a note demands the locket and all copies in exchange for her life. Felix must choose between evidence and the woman he loves. Beat: the theme's cruelest test — love against duty, literally priced.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix fakes compliance: he announces publicly that the locket will be 'returned to the crypt' before trial, knowing Salas must destroy it there. He salts the announcement with a forged detail only the file's true author would correct. Beat: turning the killer's archival obsession into bait.

chapters.title: Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Night. Salas enters the crypt to burn the locket and finds Felix waiting with Ibarra; Marisol, freed earlier, locks the door behind them. Salas confesses — the murders, the forgeries, a lifetime guarding a lie he inherited as a boy. Beat: climax, quiet and terrible.

chapters.title: Testimony in Ink
chapters.summary: Trial opens. Felix testifies with the reconstructed register, the granddaughter's affidavit, and the locket chain of custody. Salas pleads out rather than let the founder's myth be dismantled in open court. Beat: justice achieved but truth partially re-buried.

chapters.title: Reinterment
chapters.summary: Months later, the town buries actual remains under Vidal's name and a truer stone. Felix catalogs the case file, closes it, and lets Marisol read the last page — his own account, ending with her name. Beat: inheritance redefined as what we choose to keep.
